subject: Archaeology
title: The Dead Sea Scrolls
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: The Dead Sea Scrolls.

hook.text: In 1947, a Bedouin shepherd threw a rock into a cave and heard a clay jar shatter. Inside were ancient scrolls.

buildup.text: The scrolls contained the oldest known copies of Hebrew Bible texts, dating back over 2,000 years.

discovery.text: Over 900 manuscripts were found in 11 caves near the Dead Sea, written between 250 BCE and 68 CE.

twist.text: Some scrolls were sold on the antiquities black market before scholars even knew they existed.

climax.text: The scrolls showed that biblical texts had been copied with astonishing accuracy for two millennia.

punchline.text: A thrown rock revealed the oldest Bible texts ever found.

quiz.question: How were the Dead Sea Scrolls discovered?
options: A team of archaeologists located them using ground-penetrating radar
A Bedouin shepherd accidentally found them in a cave
They were hidden in a temple and found during renovation
